title: One weekend, three plans
text: At thirty, three plans land on one weekend. {friend.first} needs a hand, an old group wants to meet, and the quiet afternoon you promised yourself is looking popular.

outcomes.text: I helped {friend.first}, and we found time to catch up while the boxes waited.

choices.label: Choose one gathering and say no to the rest

outcomes.text: I chose the people I missed most and declined the other plans kindly. The weekend felt like mine again.
I rushed between plans and enjoyed none of them properly. Next time, the calendar gets a vote.

title: The weekend you chose
text: A note from the year you turned thirty brings back that crowded weekend with {friend.first}. The plans mattered less than the people in them.

choices.label: Make another plan, with room to breathe

outcomes.text: We found a day that worked for both of us and left the rest of the calendar blank.

choices.label: Keep the note and the memory

outcomes.text: I kept the note. It reminded me that saying no can protect a yes.

title: A place at the little table
text: The classroom feels enormous at five. {teacher.first} points out an empty seat, while {classmate.first} is making a tower from blocks and pure confidence.

outcomes.text: The tower leaned, fell, and was rebuilt. We made room for each other's ideas.
I learned the room before I joined the game. {teacher.first} said that was fine.
{teacher.first} helped me settle in, then let me choose when to join.

title: The first classroom memory
text: A familiar kind of classroom smell brings back that first day. {classmate.first} and {teacher.first} helped the room feel smaller.

choices.label: Remember who made space for me

outcomes.text: I kept the memory of being welcomed. Small kindnesses can change a whole day.

choices.label: Be that person for someone else

outcomes.text: I noticed someone hanging back and made room beside me.

title: The project nobody owns
text: The class project is due soon. {classmate.first} has ideas, {teacher.first} wants a plan, and the group's shared document is mostly a picture of a dog.

outcomes.text: The plan worked. {classmate.first} did the research, I kept the group moving, and {teacher.first} praised the result.
The parts fit together at the last minute. It was not elegant, but everyone contributed.
The project looked polished. I was tired, and {classmate.first} felt left out.
{teacher.first} helped us split the work. We lost a little time, but nobody had to carry the whole group.

title: A project from years ago
text: An old class folder turns up. {classmate.first} and {teacher.first} are in the notes beside a plan that began with a dog picture.

choices.label: Keep the notes as a reminder

outcomes.text: I kept the page. Learning to work with people mattered as much as the grade.
I shared what worked with someone facing a group project of their own.

title: The unwritten work guide
text: The routine sheet skips three steps. {coworker.first} offers to show you how the team really does it.

choices.label: Learn the routine and write it down

outcomes.text: I learned the shortcuts, then made a guide the next new starter could use.
The guide helped, though the first draft needed a few corrections from {coworker.first}.

choices.label: Ask questions as they come up

outcomes.text: It took longer, but {coworker.first} appreciated that I checked instead of guessing.
I found my own way through it. A few avoidable mistakes made the week longer.

title: The guide gets used
text: A new starter asks about the routine you once had to learn. You remember {coworker.first} showing you the ropes.

outcomes.text: I passed on what {coworker.first} taught me. The team had one less mystery to solve.
I sent them the notes. It was enough to get through the day.

title: The knowledge gap
text: A teammate is leaving, and half the team's routine lives in {coworker.first}'s head. The handover has one short week left.

outcomes.text: We wrote down the steps that mattered and left space for questions. The next person had a fair start.

choices.label: Ask for time to shadow them

outcomes.text: I learned the most fragile parts of the job. The rest of my work had to wait.
I met my deadline. The next person inherited a few avoidable mysteries.

title: The handover holds up
text: A new colleague asks how the team learned the work after {coworker.first} left. The old notes are still useful, with a few updates.

outcomes.text: We kept the useful parts and fixed what had changed. A handover is a living thing.
I introduced them to the right people. Nobody should have to guess alone.

title: The noticeboard plan
text: A few neighbors want to fix the neglected noticeboard. {neighbor.first} has paint, someone else has opinions, and nobody has checked whether the ladder is safe.

outcomes.text: We checked the ladder, shared the jobs, and left the board better than we found it.
The board is fixed. It took two tries and three opinions about the shade of blue.
I left the paint with {neighbor.first}. The small contribution was still useful.
I had other things to do. The board stayed crooked for another month.

title: Still on the board
text: The noticeboard you helped with is still in use. {neighbor.first} points out a faded note from the first workday.

outcomes.text: I posted a useful update. Small things make a place feel shared.

choices.label: Let someone else take the lead

outcomes.text: I left space for the next person with an idea.
